question: What tariffs did the US announce on 'Liberation Day' in April 2025?
text:
On **April 2, 2025**, which President Donald Trump called **“Liberation Day,”** the U.S. announced two tiers of new import tariffs: a **10% baseline tariff** on most imports starting **April 5**, and **higher “reciprocal” tariffs** for selected trading partners scheduled to start **April 9**. The higher rates replaced the 10% baseline for those partners; they weren’t added on top of it, though other existing duties could still apply. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/04/regulating-imports-with-a-reciprocal-tariff-to-rectify-trade-practices-that-contribute-to-large-and-persistent-annual-united-states-goods-trade-deficits/?trk=public_post_comment-text&utm_source=openai))

| Trading partner | Tariff announced April 2 |
|---|---:|
| United Kingdom | 10% |
| European Union | 20% |
| Japan | 24% |
| South Korea | 25% |
| India | 26% |
| Taiwan | 32% |
| China | 34% |
| Vietnam | 46% |
| Cambodia | 49% |
| Lesotho | 50% |

These are selected rates from the original announcement. **Canada and Mexico** were excluded from this tariff package and remained subject to separate rules. The order also exempted certain goods, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and steel, aluminum, and autos already covered by separate tariffs. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/eo-14257.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The announced rates didn’t stay in place as planned: on **April 9**, the administration announced a 90-day pause on most higher country-specific rates, returning them to 10% effective **April 10**, while raising the rate on China. ([ustr.gov](https://www.ustr.gov/trade-topics/presidential-tariff-actions?utm_source=openai))
